answer: Copper-weighted lantern attestations. Each identity must post a unique physical token whose serial is signed into a public ledger; the token burns a hollow identifier space so duplicate serials collide and void both entries. Registration also requires solving a per-serial puzzle tied to a hardware nonce, costing roughly one hour of compute plus the token’s scrap value. A clone must acquire a fresh token and redo the work, making every marginal duplicate strictly negative-EV.
